decisions.basis: Case 0044 dossier: NL3 endpoint clause; exact transition:line:36 from InMotion to EmergencyStopping; empty trigger set and guard R45RouteToken == 7; Obstacle_Detected consumed only on nested transitions.

The exact bound entry transition:line:36 has no trigger and is guarded by R45RouteToken == 7, while the supplied event-consumer facts place Obstacle_Detected on nested transitions rather than this entry carrier. The proposed route-control lowering is only a possibility and has no supplied equivalence fact, so it is not a competent surviving defeater.
decisions.violated_obligation: Obstacle detection must cause entry into EmergencyStopping through the exact bound transition.

decisions.basis: Case 0044 dossier: NL3 action clause; exact state:EmergencyStopping:line:31; its supplied lifecycle action is EmergencyStopSendObstacleDetected, with no separate exact Emergency Stop action reference.
decisions.reason: The clause requires the exact action Emergency Stop in EmergencyStopping. The bound state contains the composite abstract action EmergencyStopSendObstacleDetected, but the supplied typed facts do not establish whether that composite action is semantically equivalent to the independently required Emergency Stop action. The composite-name interpretation remains compatible with the facts, so it is a surviving undercutting reading.

decisions.violated_obligation: EmergencyStopping must include the exact Emergency Stop action.

A child-region or guarded routing edge would not satisfy the specified default-entry property, so no competent defeater survives.

issues.basis: NL3 endpoint contract; source transition tr_0007; inspection transition line 36 has guard R45RouteToken == 7 and empty triggers; event-consumer facts place Obstacle_Detected on nested transitions lines 25-29.
issues.expected: Obstacle detection causes entry into EmergencyStopping.
issues.observed: Transition line 36 enters EmergencyStopping only under guard R45RouteToken == 7 and has no trigger; Obstacle_Detected is not a trigger on that carrier.
issues.reason: The exact closed transition into EmergencyStopping is guard-driven with no trigger, while Obstacle_Detected is consumed only by nested transitions. The entry endpoint exists, but the causal obstacle-triggered entry obligation is not closed.
issues.requirement_quote: When an obstacle is detected, the system enters the EmergencyStopping state, which includes the actions "Emergency Stop" and sends the "Obstacle Detected" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Route-control lowering could preserve causal behavior outside the trigger field, but no supplied fact establishes that equivalence.
issues.title: EmergencyStopping entry trigger mismatch

issues.basis: NL3 action contract; source EmergencyStopping lifecycle; closed state line 31 contains during abstract EmergencyStopSendObstacleDetected; working-contract mapping identifies one composite compiler-owned action.
issues.expected: EmergencyStopping includes the exact action Emergency Stop.
issues.observed: EmergencyStopping carries abstract action EmergencyStopSendObstacleDetected, with no separate exact action ref for Emergency Stop.
issues.reason: The closed EmergencyStopping state contains one composite abstract lifecycle action rather than a separately bound exact Emergency Stop action carrier. The source requires Emergency Stop as an independent action, so the exact action value is not closed.
issues.requirement_quote: When an obstacle is detected, the system enters the EmergencyStopping state, which includes the actions "Emergency Stop" and sends the "Obstacle Detected" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The composite action name includes the required concept, but the supplied closure does not establish equivalence to an independently required action.
issues.title: EmergencyStop action semantic gap

issues.basis: NL3 effect contract; source lifecycle and effect phrase; closed state line 31 action EmergencyStopSendObstacleDetected; no separate state effect field is supplied.
issues.expected: EmergencyStopping sends the Obstacle Detected signal.
issues.observed: The closed state has composite abstract action EmergencyStopSendObstacleDetected; no independently typed Obstacle Detected state effect is present.
issues.reason: The source requires a send effect, while the closed state exposes a composite abstract lifecycle action rather than a separately typed output effect.
issues.requirement_quote: When an obstacle is detected, the system enters the EmergencyStopping state, which includes the actions "Emergency Stop" and sends the "Obstacle Detected" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The composite lifecycle action may encode the output, but the supplied typed facts do not prove that interpretation.
issues.title: Obstacle Detected output semantic gap

issues.basis: NL5 initial-entry contract; source requires Accelerating; closed transition line 18 targets UnspecifiedInitial line 17; inspection reports Accelerating unreachable and UnspecifiedInitial reachable.
issues.expected: The InMotion-owned initial edge enters Accelerating.
issues.observed: InMotion initial transition line 18 enters UnspecifiedInitial.
issues.reason: The exact InMotion-owned initial edge targets synthetic UnspecifiedInitial rather than the required Accelerating state.
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the Accelerating substate, moving to the Cruising substate once cruising speed is reached, as indicated by the "Reached Cruising/Cruise" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: An InMotion initial edge exists, but its exact target is the synthetic state rather than Accelerating.
issues.title: InMotion initial child mismatch

issues.basis: NL8 scoped initial-entry contract; source InMotion owner and Accelerating target; closed transition line 18; Accelerating is unreachable from top-level initial entry.
issues.expected: Within InMotion, motion begins by entering Accelerating.
issues.observed: The InMotion-owned initial edge enters UnspecifiedInitial; Accelerating is not reachable from top-level initial entry.
issues.reason: The separate scoped InMotion entry obligation is not satisfied because the owner-local initial edge targets UnspecifiedInitial rather than Accelerating.
issues.requirement_quote: The system enters the Accelerating substate when motion begins, marked by the "Entry/Accelerate" action.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The model has an owner-local initial edge, but the target is the wrong state.
issues.title: InMotion entry to Accelerating mismatch

issues.basis: NL8 operating-state obligation; source/model Accelerating identity; inspection and verify facts refute reachability of Accelerating; its entry action remains present.
issues.expected: The required Accelerating operating state can be entered and perform its entry behavior.
issues.observed: Accelerating is unreachable from the top-level initial entry, although it contains entry action Accelerate.
issues.reason: The exact required Accelerating state and entry action exist, but deterministic finite reachability shows the state cannot be reached from the top-level initial entry. This is a causal operational gap distinct from the satisfied state_action property.
issues.requirement_quote: The system enters the Accelerating substate when motion begins, marked by the "Entry/Accelerate" action.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The state_action contract itself is satisfied structurally; reachability is a separate causal property and the supplied NL does not provide a standalone reachability contract.
issues.title: Accelerating reachability gap

issues.basis: NL9 effect contract; source lifecycle effect; FCSTM Approaching line 14 has during abstract Send; inspection action inventory contains Send but no state-effect row.
issues.observed: Approaching carries abstract during action Send; no separately typed signal effect is closed.
issues.reason: The closed model carries Send as a during lifecycle action, but the exact contract property is a signal effect and no separately typed state-effect fact is supplied.
issues.requirement_quote: In the Approaching substate, the system sends the "Send" signal and continues to approach the destination.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The during action named Send may represent the required signal, but the supplied closure does not establish action/effect equivalence.
issues.title: Approaching send effect semantic gap

issues.basis: NL3 derived trigger contract; source transition tr_0007; FCSTM event Obstacle_Detected and transition line 36; inspection line 36 has empty triggers and guard R45RouteToken == 7.
issues.expected: The EmergencyStopping entry transition is triggered by the obstacle-detected event.
issues.observed: The exact entry transition line 36 has no triggers; Obstacle_Detected is consumed only by nested transitions lines 25-29.
issues.reason: The exact source event and EmergencyStopping entry carrier are bound, but the closed transition has no trigger and instead depends on a route-control guard. The event is consumed only by nested transitions, not by the entry carrier.
issues.requirement_quote: When an obstacle is detected, the system enters the EmergencyStopping state, which includes the actions "Emergency Stop" and sends the "Obstacle Detected" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Route-control lowering could theoretically preserve event causality, but no supplied fact closes that equivalence.
issues.title: Obstacle event trigger mismatch

issues.basis: Source root initial transition tr_0001; closed inspection initial-entry transition:line:37 targets state:DoorsClosing:line:8; nested transition:line:18 targets state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:17.
issues.expected: The system-level initial entry targets DoorsClosing.
issues.observed: The top-level initial edge targets DoorsClosing; the separate InMotion-owned initial edge targets UnspecifiedInitial.
issues.reason: The root initial edge enters DoorsClosing, satisfying the required system entry target; however, the closed model also contains an independent nested InMotion initial edge that enters the synthetic UnspecifiedInitial state rather than the required Accelerating state. This nested defect is evaluated under the separate NL5 contract.
issues.requirement_quote: The system starts in the DoorsClosing state and transitions to InMotion when the doors are closed, triggered by the "Closed/SendDeparted" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The model has a valid top-level initial edge to DoorsClosing, so the supplied system-level obligation itself is satisfied; the observed nested defect belongs to NL5 and should not be attributed to this contract.
issues.title: Incorrect root initial target

issues.basis: NL5 requires InMotion to enter Accelerating; source inventory binds Accelerating to InMotion; closed inspection transition:line:18 is owned by InMotion and targets state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:17; finite reachability also shows Accelerating is unreachable from the top-level initial entry.
issues.expected: The initial edge owned by InMotion targets Accelerating.
issues.observed: The exact InMotion initial edge transition:line:18 targets synthetic state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:17; Accelerating is not reachable from the top-level initial entry.
issues.reason: The exact InMotion-owned initial edge exists but targets UnspecifiedInitial, while the source obligation requires Accelerating. The target and owner are exact, so this is a scoped initial-entry mismatch.
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the Accelerating substate, moving to the Cruising substate once cruising speed is reached, as indicated by the "Reached Cruising/Cruise" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: UnspecifiedInitial is compiler-generated and could be intended as an intermediate placeholder, but no supplied fact establishes that it semantically enters Accelerating, and the finite reachability fact explicitly leaves Accelerating unreachable.
issues.title: InMotion enters synthetic initial state
